questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Highly recognised institution, one of the leading University in the field of Nutrition Research

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Was very happy with the University and the courses I was able to attend. Unfortunately, I had troubles getting all the courses approved and signed on time by KU. This has complicated my stay and studies during my exhange

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Exchange student coordinator was very helpful and guided me through my possibilities. Otherwise I had to take the initiative to sort certain things out by myself. Orientation day was great and I provided enough information about the institution itself

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation day. Possibilities of courses, and other activities in the University

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Was great, it provided all the essential information. Of course, it was difficult in the beginning to get used to the new online platform and how things work in another place but overall, everything was perfect.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: was very difficult. I suggest other students to start searching for accommodation 3 months before they plan to go on an exhange. Since my scenario was very complicated and I was unsure until the last week of the start of my exchange, I had a very hard time finding an affordable accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: difficult transportation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very hard to find a place in general due to the high demand

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very smooth.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just had to forward all the necessary documents including LA, and my choice of subjects. Once everything was in order, I have gotten the final approval from my host institution.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange student office was available every weekday and they were ready to help if I had any problems.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: My home institution was very flexible with my choice of subjects as long as the classes did not overlap in the schedule. However, there were strict deadlines and registrations periods which didn't allow further modification afterwards,.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that you choose the right subjects at the first place, otherwise changes in the LA can take some time to be approved by both institution which could lead to missing a deadline for registration periods. Make a thorough research in the subjects and course beforehand so you don't need to make changes during your exchange.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very happy with the professionalism of the institution and the level of education.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I mainly took advanced level, MSc level courses. they were all demanding and required very active participation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of the lectures were pre recored so students had time to go through the study material in their on pace. This allowed me to prepare better and to go through the material and lectures multiple times.  There were only planned Q&A session 2x a week for each subjects where students were able to address any questions or doubts they had. I really enjoyed this way of studying.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Immunometabolism
Nutrition and Cancer 
Intro to Epidemiology and Public Health 
Miscellaneous Tools in Epic Research
Essentials of Nutritional Physiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. I really enjoyed Nutrition and Cancer and Immunometabolism

questions.answer: housing was really expensive and difficult to find. But this is due the fact that I got the final permission from Ku very last minute.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: housing and transportation

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: so many opportunities in sport and other activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there were 30 different sport clubs and many different student clubs where you could join and spend time together with other students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: try the sport facilities, they are great.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: study :D

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it was my second exchange throughout my academic years. Wur was definitely more professional than my previous experience.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: join the student clubs, they have many different themes according to your interest. Than you can find peers that have similar interests and hobbies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the dutch are reserved but still more open than Danes. They were friendly and helpful. of course the language barrier is a bit of a challenge but most people speak English fluently.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Netherlands is very multicultural, so many foreign people. It was nice to meet some many people from so many cultures. it was a very intercultural experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The level of education is more demanding than at KU. 
The university is super great, with so many possibilities in the professional field. Its challenging in the beginning but you get used it after a few weeks. the environment is very competitive. 
Great facilities, and very good student buffet :D

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
find the right courses early. Follow the structure and deadlines of the subjects and registration periods. 
Going with Erasmus and SU allows you to live ok, but I felt it was a bit more expensive overall than in Denmark.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: to receive high grades in my courses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: keep up the pace with the lectures and to deal with the competitive environment

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: go for it! I didn't regret it at all and I would do it again if I had the opportunity!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
